_comment: The locales Decoy targets. This roster is Decoy's own decision and is not derived
from any upstream corpus -- it was seeded from the set faker-js happened to carry,
but adding or dropping a locale is now an edit here rather than a consequence of
somebody else's release. Fallback chains are derived from these codes by the rule
documented on DecoyLocales.chain(for:), not stored, so they cannot drift from the roster.
`cldr` maps a Decoy code to its CLDR equivalent where the automatic rule (underscores
to hyphens, then strip trailing segments) gets it wrong. `null` means the locale has
no CLDR equivalent at all and adapters sourcing from CLDR should skip it.
Twelve locales were removed in the cut recorded in docs/corpus-strategy.md: af_ZA, dv,
eo, ku_ckb, ku_kmr_latin, mn_MN_cyrl, ne, ta_IN, th, ur, uz_UZ_latin and zu_ZA. Each
was a language root -- no same-language ancestor to inherit from -- that supplied no
personal names of its own, so every person it generated was English wearing the
locale's postcode. A regional variant like en_US or de_AT is thin for the opposite
reason and is fine: it inherits its own language. The test to re-add one is names,
not volume; ta_IN carried 15,612 native values and still could not name a person.
Re-adding is an edit here plus a source that supplies person.first_name for it.
